shorts.promoted_long_title: Why Did Franklin Fly a Kite in a Storm?
shorts.frame0_change_by_1s: Silk kite already straining against dark storm cloud at frame 0; loose hemp threads on the string stand upright by 1.0 s.

teach_overlay.band: 16:9 centre band (clear of 0–2 s hook and 9–14 s title)

rows.spoken: Franklin's kite was never hit by lightning.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 vertical crop on kite under dark storm cloud (no lightning bolt hitting kite); hook caption NEVER HIT IT at 0.0–2.0 s.

rows.spoken: In seventeen fifty-two he flew it into a storm cloud, holding a dry silk ribbon inside a shed.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 crop on Franklin inside the shed holding the dry silk ribbon tied to the key; WHEN stamp 'PHILADELPHIA · 1752' at 2.7–6.2 s.

rows.spoken: The loose threads of the twine stood up on end. He brought his knuckle to the key, and a spark jumped across.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 crop on twine threads rising (9.14–12.10 s) then knuckle drawing a small spark from the brass key (12.10–16.78 s); promoted long title on screen 9.0–14.0 s.

rows.spoken: If lightning had struck the kite, he would almost certainly have died.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 crop on the storm cloud above the shed, returning in the final 4 s (18.24–22.24 s) to the opening kite plate for seamless loop.

shorts.youtube_title: How Does a Lightning Rod Work?
shorts.promoted_long_title: Why Did Franklin Fly a Kite in a Storm?
shorts.frame0_change_by_1s: Pointed iron rod on a steep roof under a dark cloud at frame 0; rain sweeps across the slates by 1.0 s.

teach_overlay.band: 16:9 centre band (clear of 0–2 s hook and 9–14 s title)

rows.spoken: That thin metal rod on top of tall buildings was Benjamin Franklin's idea.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 vertical crop on pointed iron lightning rod rising above a roof; hook caption ONE THIN ROD at 0.0–2.0 s.

rows.spoken: Lightning takes the easiest path to the ground. A wooden roof is a terrible path, so it bursts into flame. A metal rod is an easy one.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 crop on theKEEP £0 code graphics (P5:08/09/10) + roof plate; promoted long title card on screen 9.0–14.0 s.

rows.spoken: The lightning runs down the rod, round the building, and into the earth.
rows.crop_9x16: 9:16 crop on SAFE PATH DOWN diagram / wire running down outer wall into earth.

rows.spoken: Some towers are struck over twenty times a year.
rows.crop_9x16: DATA overlay '20+ STRIKES A YEAR' at 20.6–24.0 s over the opening roof-rod plate so the final 4 s loop seamlessly.
